report:
Fresh followup review of meta.reviews.validation_layout. Preserved the prior input/output, started fresh and read the full claim, sole ordinary implementation association and all four ordinary test bodies. Recaptured prior fixture helpers (review tests lines 1–104), valid_anchor_name dependency (spec.rs lines 245–259), and check.rs orchestration. Compared all prior/current fragments by path/selector and implementation/test metadata. review.rs only gained a placeholder_status association comment. The spec.rs fixed line range shifted its incidental boundary context by one line, adding the preceding output.push_str and dropping the following markdown_files signature; the complete valid_anchor_name helper remains present and unchanged. All other captured contents and this anchor's association metadata are unchanged, with no removed captures. I reassessed this delta against the complete previous assessment, not a blind verdict refresh.

The associated start path in review.rs implements one current workspace/validations/<complete dotted ID> directory. anchor_directory uses valid_anchor_name to reject invalid ASCII identifier components and separators; start verifies that the valid ID exists in current inventory before resetting it. Under the directory lock it removes the old anchor directory, creates the current directory, writes input.json captured context and summary.json identity/start metadata with an unset recording timestamp. The old input/output are discarded, not retained as review history. record validates summary and captured-input freshness, writes output.json assessment and marks the summary recorded. load_saved accepts output only for recorded summaries. read_summary requires real directory identity matching the complete anchor ID; read_json requires regular files and valid JSON; load_saved rejects invalid directory IDs. validate/acceptable keep unfinished and malformed reviews failing, as exercised through the captured check.rs orchestration. The fixture operates on real temporary Cargo/model/spec/filesystem layouts.

All four associated tests expose relevant assertions. start_invalidates_previous_success_and_record_is_required creates a valid previous report, restarts, compares saved/returned input, checks summary identity and null recording time, output absence, one unfinished loaded record and failed gate; recording after an appended read preserves input bytes and restores validity, while later record/read attempts fail. completed_corrupt_records_and_invalid_layout_cannot_pass deletes each required file, supplies malformed/blank/extra-field reports and a non-directory entry; both library and CLI checks must fail with the expected anchor and reason. invalid_ids_and_paths_are_rejected_without_destroying_existing_reports tests traversal, absolute/slashed names, empty dotted components and an unknown valid ID, requiring rejection and preservation of the existing output bytes. Its remaining path/selector rejection assertions additionally preserve active captured context. unsupported_versions_and_mismatched_identity_cannot_pass corrupts the summary identity and each version independently and checks the specific mismatch/version diagnostic. Together these assertions cover naming, directory-summary agreement, reset/invalidation, the three-file roles and completed-record requirements.

No TODO or N/A entries exist. The marker and incidental line-range-boundary changes do not change behavior or adequacy; the helper remains fully captured. No source edits, formatting, tests or workspace build were performed in this followup. Commands executed were review start/read, capture comparison and record. Central/previous execution was not represented as new execution. No requested edits.
